findings.message:
Escape digit patterns in the RFC-850 regex

The template literal uses `\d` as a single backslash escape, which is cooked to `d` before `RegExp` receives it. Consequently, `RFC850_DATE` matches literal `d` characters rather than digits, so valid RFC-850 dates are never resolved and the runtime's default two-digit-year parsing remains in effect. Use `\\d` in the template literal (as in `HTTP_DATE`).

src/github/rate-limit.ts:57-58

summary: RFC-850 year resolution is disabled by incorrectly escaped regex patterns.
